# Problem 1

```{r birthday-function}
birthday_match <- function(n_people) {
  birthdays <- sample(1:365, size = n_people, replace = TRUE)
  
  any(duplicated(birthdays))
}
```
```{r birthday-simulation}
set.seed(123)

birthday_results <- tibble(
  group_size = 2:50
) %>%
  mutate(
    probability = map_dbl(
      group_size,
      function(n_people) {
        mean(replicate(10000, birthday_match(n_people)))
      }
    )
  )

birthday_results %>%
  filter(group_size %in% c(2, 23, 50)) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```
```{r birthday-plot}
ggplot(birthday_results, aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2C7FB8", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(color = "#2C7FB8", size = 1.5) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0.5,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey50"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of a shared birthday",
    x = "Number of people",
    y = "Estimated probability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

The estimated probability of at least two people sharing a birthday
increases as the group size increases. It is about 51% for a group
of 23 people and about 97% for a group of 50 people. Larger groups
contain more pairs of people, which creates more opportunities
for a shared birthday.

# Problem 2

```{r read-participant-files}
participant_files <- tibble(
  file_name = list.files("data", pattern = "\\.csv$")
) %>%
  mutate(
    data = map(
      file_name,
      function(current_file) {
        read_csv(
          file.path("data", current_file),
          show_col_types = FALSE
        )
      }
    )
  )

participant_files
```

```{r tidy-study-data}
study_tidy <- participant_files %>%
  mutate(
    participant_id = str_remove(file_name, "\\.csv$")
  ) %>%
  separate(
    participant_id,
    into = c("arm", "subject_id"),
    sep = "_",
    remove = FALSE
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    arm = recode(
      arm,
      con = "Control",
      exp = "Experimental"
    )
  ) %>%
  unnest(cols = data) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("week_"),
    names_to = "week",
    names_prefix = "week_",
    names_transform = list(week = as.integer),
    values_to = "observation"
  ) %>%
  select(participant_id, arm, subject_id, week, observation)

study_tidy %>%
  slice_head(n = 8) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r study-spaghetti-plot}
ggplot(
  study_tidy,
  aes(
    x = week,
    y = observation,
    group = participant_id,
    color = arm
  )
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 1.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ arm) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Control" = "#2C7FB8",
      "Experimental" = "#D95F0E"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Individual trajectories over eight weeks",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Observation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Each line represents one participant's observations over eight weeks. The control group shows fluctuations over time without a clear overall upward trend. In the experimental group, observations generally increase over time and are higher than those in the control group during the later weeks. Both groups show differences between participants and week-to-week variation.
